gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-noto-sans-mongol: That wide-open mouth on Shantell Sans, drawn with a single fixed nib width, gives it a hand-made, slightly cheeky face. Noto Sans Mongolian sits beside it with flared terminals, modern and quiet.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-noto-sans-new-ta: Shantell Sans draws wire-like monoline letters with a wide, open mouth, and Noto Sans New Tai Lue follows in sans-serif curves that look cupped rather than clenched. Loose play meets rounded restraint.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-noto-sans-nko: Spaghetti-like strokes of one width give Shantell Sans its wide-mouthed, doodled charm. Noto Sans NKo, a plain sans with see-through c openings, would carry a long passage smoothly, letting the heading's quirks stay a pleasant surprise instead of a chore.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-noto-sans-old-so: Shantell Sans glides under the eye like bent wire, its mouth wide and its line never changing width. It excels at personality, while Noto Sans Old South Arabian handles friendly, clean text with curved strokes that stop before turning inward.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-noto-sans-shavia: Shantell Sans looks laser-cut from a sheet, every stroke made with one cutting width and a wide, open mouth. Its quirky outlines meet Noto Sans Shavian, a plain sans whose rope-loose curves never knot at the ends, and the result is lively yet tidy.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-ojuju: Expressive from the first line, Shantell Sans keeps its stroke flat and unmodulated, with a mouth wide as a cut tin lid. Ojuju, a plain sans with a faint spring-wire contrast and wide s curves, would read friendly and smooth across many lines.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-overpass: Overpass is a modern sans with crisp, unblotted e shapes. Shantell Sans, with its wide mouth and fixed nib width, adds the playful display voice, so bump up Overpass's size a little to hold its own.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-palanquin: Cable bent into shapes, that is Shantell Sans, with a wide mouth and no swelling or thinning. Palanquin, a sans with curved letters and wide, unclosed mouths, gives it a contemporary, tidy partner, and their shared openness is the strongest link.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-philosopher: Pen pressure never changes in Shantell Sans, so its wide-mouthed letters look hand-drawn and a bit playful. Philosopher, a sans with soft thick-thin shifts and curves full of daylight, steps in to keep the text clean and gentle.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-gf-pontano-sans: Expressive describes Shantell Sans, whose twine-like strokes press into the page at a single width with a wide mouth. But Pontano Sans does the quieter job, setting text with wide open c terminals in a contemporary, professional way.
